A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRANSPORTER study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated equations and renumbered qualitative galleries.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation evaluations across three VLMs, quantitative comparisons, component ablations, timing measurements and qualitative experiments in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds qualitative coupling comparisons and experiments examining counting, role reversal and spatial plausibility.

M1.justification: The coupling modules, rho-OT Algorithm 1, concept-bank objective, frozen backbones and inference procedure are retained. The rewritten logit notation does not establish an actual algorithm change; the mathematical ambiguity is noted under T1.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation datasets remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 11 adds qualitative scenarios involving agent-role reversal and implausible on/under-chair relations. Flower picking also extends the existing counting examples to a case requiring an additional action; the cited benchmarks are not themselves newly evaluated.

E2.justification: The AM, GradViT, MACO, LEAPS, OT and component-ablation comparator sets are retained. Figure 8's decode-and-re-encode comparator corresponds to the existing inference-only ablation in v1; Table 3's renamed row has identical results.

E3.justification: New Figure 10 compares the three VLMs using common prompts, matching modulation endpoints and the same inference seed. This adds a controlled qualitative comparison design. Existing dataset allocations, model sizes, training budgets, metrics and quantitative evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 8 adds qualitative evidence about scene preservation with learned coupling versus decode-and-re-encode inference. Supplementary Section 11 and Figure 10 add targeted counting, role-reversal and spatial-plausibility case studies, including failures. Existing ablations and sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 10 newly specifies inference seed 0 shared across VLMs. Existing multiseed averaging statements and Table 7's three-run timing protocol remain unchanged. No increased run count, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Numerical results in the corresponding tables remain unchanged. New qualitative results show scene preservation relative to decode-and-re-encode inference and unsuccessful role-reversal and under-chair modulations. These are additional findings, not improved scores under the existing quantitative settings.

T1.justification: The continuous and discrete OT objectives are relocated unchanged to supplementary Section 6. However, v1's Equation 11 explicitly aggregates two probability-coordinate differences, whereas v2 uses an absolute-difference expression with compressed omega symbols. Their scalar/vector meaning and aggregation are insufficiently explicit to determine whether this is equivalent shorthand or a revised divergence definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: introducing L2V, coupling visual and semantic spaces, learning logit-controlled concept vectors, and producing visually detailed, semantically aligned explanations.

C2.justification: New Section 11 interprets counting difficulty through the need for additional actions, role-reversal failures through missed linguistic relationships, and under-chair outputs through spatial deficiencies or learned priors. The earlier limitations concerning entangled concepts and the discrete concept bank are retained.

D1.justification: The implementation sections retain the same architectures, hyperparameters, dataset sample counts, optimization schedules and timing hardware information. The project address points to the same resource; adding its HTTPS prefix does not establish changed access or availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations on VLM interpretation, counting and spatial-language failures, including VALSE, What's Up and Vision Language Models Are Blind, plus flow-model references. It removes the original Phi-4 report and a normalizing-flows review. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits explanatory prose, streamlines logit notation, moves the OT formulations into the supplement, and transfers existing Figure 7 discussions from Ablations to Examples. It also adds the phenomena discussion and acknowledgments while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 8 and 10, revises Figure 2's annotations, and reflows equations and tables. The earlier supplementary galleries remain as Figures 11–14, with image compression changes. Section 11 mistakenly references Figure 9 for the panels captioned Figure 10.

improvement.justification: The added coupling comparison and explicit failure cases provide useful evidence about the method's behavior and make the empirical account more balanced. The improvement is limited: quantitative validation is unchanged, the new analyses are qualitative, and the compressed Hellinger notation and mismatched figure references reduce clarity.
